summary: Round-2 pre-launch re-review of notes/sim10_ada_baseline_20261110 at 58894c331 (runtime still PR #298 head 67c327a1; no framework edits). The round-1 blocker ADA-01 is closed: run.sbatch now requests --ntasks=3 --cpus-per-task=16 (48 CPUs preserved), matching the `mpiexec -n 3` launch in campaign.py:56, and support.affinity() still trims every rank to the same first 24 physical cores. The new GPU-selection logic (campaign.py:26-33) takes the first entry of the scheduler's CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES mask, resolves it via `nvidia-smi -i` to exactly one L40S UUID, records the full allocation mask, inventory and chosen UUID in provenance.json, and exposes only that UUID as JF_GPU_UUID; gpu_tests.py:9 and runner.py:7 set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES from it (ranks 0-1 masked to ''), getDeviceCount()==1 is asserted in both, and audit.py:31 requires device.mask == provenance gpu_uuid. ADA-03 is closed: audit.py:35-42 now checks every recorded runtime_files entry against the frozen receipt (Python paths must lie under the PR source and match receipt['python']; natives must match receipt['native']), and test_audit.py adds 1 accepting + 13 mutation tests including python_hash/native_hash corruptions applied consistently across all rows so cross-row equality cannot hide a receipt mismatch. ADA-04 is closed for sources: prepare_runtime.py:11 compares psana, xtcdata and psalg native sources and records build-configuration hashes; however the committed native-compatibility-summary.json shows psana/meson.build differs between PR and frozen build (pr 4cd07821…, frozen 27ae0bce…) while prepare_runtime only records (never asserts) config equality and README/scope/response describe the config hashes as 'recorded separately' without disclosing the mismatch. This is raised as new ADA-08 (medium, non-blocking for launch, must be resolved before results acceptance). ADA-05 closed: runtime.py:18 asserts find_spec('psana.psexp.parallel_pread') is None and the limitation is documented; this checkout's psana/meson.build builds no parallel_pread extension and it is used only by debugtools. BDS-02 is partially hardened: run_owned (campaign.py:7-19) launches gpu_tests/mpiexec in a new session and on any exception TERMs the process group, waits 15 s, then KILLs and reaps before the finally reaches rmtree; test_campaign.py covers success/nonzero/timeout-reap; the staging-phase hard-kill orphan risk and manual recovery are documented in README/scope. ADA-02, ADA-06 and ADA-07 are closed by documentation as agreed (20-min budget with incomplete-on-timeout semantics, retained tmp/CuPy/pytest caches, SMD warm / JF-only cold gate / no cache-fraction inference). The automatic post-campaign audit is wired in run.sbatch:35 and will not run if the campaign exits nonzero (set -e), which is acceptable because audit requires complete.json. One new low item (ADA-09): audit.py:35 derives the PR source root from the unresolved receipt['source'] string while identity() records resolve()d paths, so a symlinked attempt path would make a valid run fail the audit (fail-closed only). No regressions found in campaign/runner/support/bulk_accounting relative to round 1; the matrix, settings, accounting, timer/NIC bracket and cold-gate logic are unchanged. This pass covers code readiness only: GPU acceptance (gpu-tests.json with no skips) and measured performance remain pending the allocation, and no rates are approved.
checks: Read review-01/review.json and review-01/response.md and mapped each prior finding (ADA-01..07, BDS-02) to the current code and docs.

run.sbatch: --ntasks=3 --cpus-per-task=16 --gres=gpu:l40s:1 --exclusive --mem=128G --time=00:20:00 --signal=B:TERM@120; TERM/INT traps propagate to the campaign child; audit.py runs after campaign into $attempt/audit.json; TMPDIR/CUPY_CACHE_DIR under the shared-scratch attempt directory (ADA-06 documented).

campaign.py: run_owned uses start_new_session=True, killpg(SIGTERM) -> 15 s wait -> killpg(SIGKILL) -> reap on any BaseException (timeout, nonzero, SystemExit from SIGTERM handler); gpu_tests (300 s) and each mpiexec case (900 s) launched through it; stage rmtree + cleanup.json in finally unchanged.

campaign.py GPU selection: first element of the Slurm CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES mask -> nvidia-smi -i -> exactly one row containing 'L40S' -> UUID exported as JF_GPU_UUID; provenance records allocation_gpu_mask, gpu_inventory, gpu_uuid, cpu_affinity, staged files, mount, harness hashes and the full native receipt.

runner.py: ranks 0-1 get CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' and rank 2 gets the UUID before any import; activate() precedes mpi4py/psana imports; getDeviceCount()==1; device.mask recorded; 13 modules passed to identity(); matrix/accounting/timer/NIC/cold-gate logic unchanged from round 1.

runtime.py: activate() requires receipt status pass + pr_sha, refuses if psana already imported, two search locations [PR source, frozen psana], and asserts find_spec('psana.psexp.parallel_pread') is None; identity() resolves paths and checks Python under PR source with receipt hash, natives against receipt['native'].

prepare_runtime.py: ls-files now covers psana, xtcdata, psalg for .pyx/.pxd/.cc/.hh/.h/.cpp/.c/.cu with byte-equality asserted; build-configuration files (meson.build, meson_options.txt, CMakeLists.txt, setup.py, setup.cfg, pyproject.toml) hashed for pr and frozen but equality is NOT asserted.

native-compatibility-summary.json: 225 native sources, 961 Python files, 28 natives; all build-configuration pairs equal except psana/meson.build (pr 4cd07821… vs frozen 27ae0bce…). No disclosure of this mismatch in README.md, scope.md, response.md or validation.json.

psana/meson.build at this checkout: builds dgram, container, shmem, peakFinder_ext, psalg_ext, peakfinder8, constFracDiscrim, dgramCreate, dgramchunk, smdreader, eventbuilder, parallelreader, dgramedit, quadanode, dgramlite, hsd, ndarray, utilsdetector_ext, optional hexanode_ext; no parallel_pread extension (only psana/setup.py.old references it); parallel_pread imported only by debugtools via try/except.

audit.py: adds per-module receipt check (lines 35-42) on top of cross-row/cross-case runtime_files equality; assigned-GPU check against provenance gpu_uuid; all other 26 checks from round 1 retained. support.require raises ValueError (jf_raw_cache_20261109/common.py:24-25), matching pytest.raises(ValueError) in test_audit.py.

test_audit.py: fixture builds a complete six-case evidence set; 13 mutation kinds (gpu skip, matrix, streams, reads, drain, assigned_gpu, cache, nic, harness, complete, cleanup, python_hash, native_hash); hash mutations applied to every row of every case so equality checks cannot mask them. test_campaign.py: success/nonzero return and timeout-reap (ProcessLookupError after wait).

validation.json/status.json: 16 harness tests (1.55 s), 2 cleanup tests, 1023 CPU unit tests (6.55 s) with runtime.activate()+identity() exercised for seven modules, syntax and bash -n pass; GPU and performance pending. runtime.sh exports PS_PARALLEL=mpi PS_FAKESTEP_FLAG=0 PS_SMD_N_EVENTS=1000 matching runner asserts and audit smd_events=1000.

Documentation: scope.md and README.md now state 20-min budget breakdown and incomplete-on-timeout semantics (ADA-02), SMD warm/JF-only cold gate and uncontrolled backend caches (ADA-07), retained caches (ADA-06), FFB orphan recovery (BDS-02), parallel_pread omission and psalg/config coverage with existing-build reuse (ADA-04/05).
limitations: No commands were run; test results (16 harness, 2 cleanup, 1023 CPU unit), syntax checks, the native-source comparison and the Slurm --test-only acceptance are taken from validation.json, status.json, native-compatibility-summary.json and the coordinator statement.

Reads of the PR source checkout ($attempt/pr-source), the frozen build tree (pr187-pr208-integration-20261026-r1/B, including its psana/meson.build), the full native-compatibility.json receipt, FFB and fixture paths were denied by the restricted file tools; the psana/meson.build mismatch is known only from the committed summary hashes and its content could not be diffed.
Framework hook semantics and psana/meson.build content were verified against this master checkout (58894c331), not the PR source tree the job will load.
Whether the shared-scratch attempt path contains symlinks (relevant to ADA-09) cannot be determined from files.
GPU acceptance tests and performance measurements are pending the allocation; nothing measured is approved by this review and Slurm account/partition/GRES validity cannot be checked from files.

findings.evidence: build_configurations['psana/meson.build'] records pr=4cd07821… and frozen=27ae0bce…, i.e. the PR's psana extension build definition differs from the one used to compile the install-B natives, while every other configuration pair matches. prepare_runtime.py:21-22 only records these hashes and never asserts equality, and README.md:55-56, scope.md:45-46 and review-01/response.md:10 describe the configuration hashes as 'recorded separately' with 'zero differences' claimed for the native comparison, so the mismatch is undisclosed. psana/meson.build defines the sources, include paths, link targets and cpp_args for dgram, smdreader, eventbuilder, shmem, container and dgramchunk, all of which this benchmark loads from install-B; a changed flag or source list there means the 'source-identical existing native extensions' claim is incomplete even though every .pyx/.cc file matches.
findings.requested_change: Before results are accepted (not required for launch): record the actual diff of psana/meson.build between the PR source and the frozen build source in the notes directory, classify whether it touches any extension_module used by this run (dgram, container, shmem, smdreader, eventbuilder, dgramchunk) or only packaging/install rules, and disclose the mismatch plus classification in README.md and scope.md. Make prepare_runtime.py either assert equality for configuration files or emit an explicit 'config_mismatches' list that audit.py checks against an allow-list, so a future config divergence cannot pass silently.

findings.evidence: audit.py builds `source=Path(receipt['source'])/'psana/psana'` from the unresolved repo path string written by prepare_runtime.py:27, then requires each recorded Python path to be relative to it and looks up receipt['python'] by relative path. runtime.identity() (runtime.py:21,25) records resolve()d paths. If the shared-scratch attempt path contains any symlink component, every valid run would fail 'Python path outside pinned PR' or 'Runtime receipt mismatch' even though identity() passed in-run. test_audit.py uses plain '/pr' paths and so does not exercise this.
findings.requested_change: In audit.py resolve the receipt source (`Path(receipt['source']).resolve()/'psana/psana'`) or have prepare_runtime.py record `str(repo.resolve())`; keep the check fail-closed. Optional: add a test with a symlinked fixture source path.
